title: Spectra Health — model length, multilingual & tooling scoping
next_steps: Redwood to share hosted vs dedicated pricing worksheet and SKU mapping
SE to run quick latency/token-cost estimate for 8k vs 32k context on two candidate models
Customer to provide a sample set of clinical notes and multilingual test prompts (EN, ES, PT)
action_items: Maya Patel (Redwood): Send SOC2 and security brief + link to private deployment whitepaper (due 2027-08-06)
Ethan Cho (Redwood SE): Run throughput/latency estimate and share cost delta table for 8k vs 32k context with quantized variants (due 2027-08-05)
Dr. Lina Gomez (Spectra): Share 200 anonymized clinical notes and multilingual prompt bank (due 2027-08-09)
summary: Initial scoping call focused on model and deployment tradeoffs for a patient-facing notes summarization and triage assistant. Key concerns: 32k context for long visit history, multilingual (English/Spanish/Portuguese), PHI handling and encryption (KMS), and tool-calling to query EHR APIs. Exploring Hosted for quick start vs Dedicated/Private for PHI compliance and deterministic latency.
topics: Security: SOC 2, audit logs, data residency
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-03 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cho (Redwood SE), Nora Li (Redwood SE), Dr. Lina Gomez (Head of ML, Spectra Health), Rahul Singh (CTO), Emma Torres (Eng Manager), Sonia Patel (Security)
---
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya, I'll run through goals real quick — want to learn about your context length needs, multilingual, and how tight latency needs are for patient triage, and then Ethan will jump into some perf considerations.
[00:18] Dr. Lina Gomez: Hi all, thanks — quick context, we are building a notes summarization + triage assistant to help nurses and intake staff. It needs to pull prior visit history, like up to 6 months of notes, sometimes long SOAP notes so context sometimes runs pretty long.
[00:36] Rahul Singh: And from infra side we care about PHI — must be encrypted at rest, KMS integration, ideally VPC peering. We're evaluating quick hosted moves for prototyping but likely need a Dedicated or Private path for the pilot.
[00:54] Maya Patel: Great, that's the typical tradeoff. Ethan, do you want to talk about model candidates and context sizing?
[01:02] Ethan Cho: Sure. So looking at open models, we usually compare mid-tier instruction-tuned models vs larger long-context variants. For 8k tokens we have good options like the 13B-class quantized variants, for 32k we either move to a dedicated long-context variant or use tiled-context trick with KV caching — but TTL, sorry, I mean KV cache management is key.
[01:22] Emma Torres: When you say tiled-context, do you mean chunking + retrieval on the client side or something the runtime handles?
[01:29] Ethan Cho: Good question. There are two patterns: client-side chunking with a retriever, or runtime-assisted prefix caching where the server keeps the KV cache for hot prefixes. Redwood supports both: you can do an explicit retrieval step or use our automatic prefix/KV caching.
[01:47] Sonia Patel: Just to interrupt — from security perspective we need audit logs for every call, SSO/SAML for access, and we need to know how long any cached prefix remains in memory since that's still a sensitive artifact.
[02:00] Nora Li: On the caching TTL, we can surface retention controls in the console and you can toggle per-model cache policies; the default keeps KV in a volatile in-memory cache not persisted to disk, and we can tie it to your KMS policies for encryption at rest for any dedicated nodes.
[02:20] Dr. Lina Gomez: Performance wise — we need sub-600ms token start latency for short queries (like triage question + patient summary) and of course throughput when batch summarizing overnight. How realistic is that on Hosted?
[02:37] Ethan Cho: For single token start you can see sub-600ms for smaller models on hosted in most regions, but if you need guaranteed SLOs Dedicated gives bandwidth. Also for 32k context generation the per-token latency may go up, so Dedicated with pinned GPU pools helps.
[02:54] Rahul Singh: Can you quantify cost difference though? We have a budget for pilots. If we pick a 32k-variant hosted, what's the delta vs 8k hosted or vs Dedicated?
[03:05] Maya Patel: We'll send a pricing worksheet — rough numbers: 32k context with a large long-context model is typically 2.5–4x per-token compute cost vs 8k on a quantized 13B. Dedicated amortizes that if you have steady throughput. We'll get Ethan to produce a short table.
[03:23] Dr. Lina Gomez: On multilingual — our patient base is 60% English, 30% Spanish, 10% Portuguese. We need parity in summarization quality. Any recommendations on models?
[03:33] Ethan Cho: Models differ. Some open instruction models have stronger Spanish support, others are English-preferred. We recommend running a small eval suite — we can run a quick bench across two or three models (one mid-size 13B quantized, one 70B compressed or 30B long context) using your sample prompts to check hallucination and English/Spanish/Portuguese scoring.
[03:54] Emma Torres: What's the effort to run that eval? We have a small dataset but it's PHI so we'd prefer redacted data.
[04:02] Maya Patel: Totally fine, redacted/anonymized samples are common. Action: Lina will share anonymized notes, Ethan will run the eval on a sandbox.
[04:12] [Speaker 1]: Uh, quick micro question — for tool calling, we need to call the EHR API to fetch lab values. Can Redwood's function/tool calling do authenticated calls with per-request credentials?
[04:26] Nora Li: Yes, you can integrate tools; we support function-style tool calls and can pass ephemeral tokens. For private deployments we can also stand up a VPC-bound connector so tokens never traverse public internet.
[04:40] Rahul Singh: How are secrets managed for that — is it integrated with our KMS?
[04:45] Ethan Cho: Yes, in Dedicated and Private you can bring your KMS or HSM. For hosted we offer managed KMS integration and we also support customer-managed keys through our enterprise plan — we can include the details in the security brief.
[04:59] Sonia Patel: Need to see the key rotation policy and proof of SOC 2 controls.
[05:05] Maya Patel: We'll attach SOC 2 and an architecture note about encryption and key rotation.
[05:12] Dr. Lina Gomez: Can we talk about model updates and versioning? We want to pin a model to avoid regressions after updates.
[05:20] Ethan Cho: Absolutely — Redwood gives version pinning and rollout policies: canary, A/B and automatic fallback to a pinned baseline. For Dedicated you can also freeze to a set model binary.
[05:33] Emma Torres: On the tool-calling flow, if the model calls the EHR tool and then generates, how do we trace that for audits? We need a per-call trace of tool inputs and outputs.
[05:44] Nora Li: We store structured traces in the console; you can export for audits. We also support token-level tracing to understand which prompt prefix contributed to the response. We can redact PHI in traces per your retention policy.
[05:59] [00:06:00] Dr. Lina Gomez: Regarding long-term storage and residency, some patients are in EU and Brazil — do you have region control?
[06:08] Maya Patel: Yes, we have multi-region hosting and Private deployments can be placed in specific cloud regions or on-prem. We'll note data residency options in the follow-up doc.
[06:18] Rahul Singh: For the 32k requirement, are you recommending a single-model approach or retrieval-augmented plus a shorter-context model?
[06:28] Ethan Cho: For many medical workflows a hybrid approach is best: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for old notes + a 8–16k context model for recent context. But if you need a strict single-pass 32k to preserve sequence and temporal order, then use a long-context variant — tradeoff is compute cost and slightly higher latency.
[06:44] Dr. Lina Gomez: Another question about hallucinations — when the model generates a medication change suggestion it would be risky. Any guardrails?
[06:52] Ethan Cho: Two things: evaluation and post-hoc classifiers/filters. We can run evals against your ground truth and tune prompts/temperature. Also Redwood supports structured output constraints and a verify step where model outputs are validated against EHR data via tool-calling before being surfaced.
[07:09] Emma Torres: Does structured output support JSON schema enforcement?
[07:12] Nora Li: Yes, schema-specified outputs are supported and you can fail/flag responses that don't match.
[07:18] [00:07:20] Sonia Patel: For compliance we'll want to log when a model output is overridden or blocked, that's non-negotiable.
[07:25] Maya Patel: Agreed, logging and overrides are available — we'll include an example trace.
[07:30] Dr. Lina Gomez: Any specific model names you recommend for multilingual medical summarization?
[07:36] Ethan Cho: Without benching, options are: 1) an instruction-tuned 13B quantized model with good multilingual fine-tuning, 2) a 30–70B long-context variant for full 32k. Names differ across vendors — we can test LlaMa-style forks, Mistral derivatives, and a few community long-context builds. We'll pick 3 candidates to run your sample prompts.
[07:57] Rahul Singh: If we choose Private deployment on-prem, what's the approximate lead time and what do you need from us?
[08:04] Nora Li: For on-prem it's typically 8–12 weeks depending on procurement, network, and security review. We need host specs, expected QPS, and a runbook for network peering. For a VPC deployment in cloud it's faster, often 2–4 weeks.
[08:18] Emma Torres: For initial pilot can we do hosted for evaluation then move to Dedicated? How smooth is that migration?
[08:25] Ethan Cho: It's designed to be smooth — same API surface, just route to dedicated capacity. There may be small model binary differences if you pin to on-prem optimized binaries, but we support migration tooling and eval harnesses.
[08:39] Maya Patel: Okay quick break down: Pilot options — A: Hosted quick prototype with redacted samples (fast), B: Hosted + Dedicated for SLA pilot, C: Private/VPC for full PHI compliance. Which resonates?
[08:56] Dr. Lina Gomez: We want to prototype quickly but keep compliance in mind — so Hosted prototype then Dedicated for pilot sounds right.
[09:05] Sonia Patel: We'll need a security review during the pilot — not a blocker but schedule earlier.
[09:11] Maya Patel: Noted. We'll put that in next steps.
[09:15] [00:09:20] Dr. Lina Gomez: For the eval, we also want multilingual metrics: ROUGE + clinical fidelity checks. Can Redwood run those?
[09:25] Ethan Cho: Yes we can compute ROUGE, BLEU, and we have a clinical hallucination scoring step where we compare generated facts to EHR visits via matching routines. We'll produce a short report.
[09:38] Rahul Singh: Also need to know about peak throughput — our triage bot might hit 200 QPS during certain windows. Can Dedicated scale?
[09:47] Nora Li: Dedicated can be configured with autoscaling policies and burst capacity; for 200 QPS we would recommend reserved pools sized to meet that SLO. We'll estimate GPU pool size in the follow-up.
[09:59] Emma Torres: Any mention of quantization options and accuracy loss? We are sensitive to hallucination changes with INT8.
[10:07] Ethan Cho: Right, quantization can slightly change output behavior. We have quantization profiles and we advise running evals on quantized binaries. Sometimes LLAMA-family models are stable with INT8, but you'll see differences and we'll surface delta metrics.
[10:20] Dr. Lina Gomez: Tooling integration — we want to chain: model calls tool, tool returns structured JSON, model synthesizes and outputs. Can we have synchronous tool calls with retries?
[10:31] Nora Li: Yes, synchronous tool calling is supported, with configurable retry/backoff policies and circuit breakers. All tool calls are traced.
[10:38] [00:10:40] Rahul Singh: For cost forecasting, can you show a projected monthly cost for a 3-month pilot with expected QPS? We can provide expected QPS and average tokens per request.
[10:48] Maya Patel: Yes, please send us expected QPS and token sizes — we'll produce a forecast sheet.
[10:53] Dr. Lina Gomez: We'll aim to provide sample QPS and token distribution by EOD tomorrow.
[10:58] Emma Torres: One last technical — latency budget is tight for interactive triage. If a long-context retrieval pipeline adds 200–300ms, does Redwood provide warm-up/keepalive to reduce cold starts?
[11:09] Ethan Cho: We support keepalive lanes and warm pools for pinned models in Dedicated, and for hosted you can use pinned routes or keepalive tokens in higher tiers. We'll add warmup recommendations in the follow-up.
[11:22] Maya Patel: Great. Anything else?
[11:25] Dr. Lina Gomez: Just curious about governance — can we tag datasets and tie model evals to dataset versions?
[11:32] Nora Li: We have eval tracking and dataset versioning in the Optimize toolkit. You'll be able to link prompt sets to eval runs and get regression alerts.
[11:43] [00:11:50] Sonia Patel: And SSO? We need SAML with SCIM provisioning.
[11:50] Maya Patel: Supported. We'll include SSO docs.
[11:53] Rahul Singh: Ok cool. Let's recap next steps.
[11:58] Maya Patel: Recap: 1) Spectra to share anonymized sample notes and QPS/token distribution; 2) Redwood SE to run multilingual eval across 3 candidate models (8k quantized, long-context 32k, mid-size 13B multilingual) and return a short report with latency/cost deltas; 3) Redwood AE to share pricing workbook and SOC2/security docs; 4) Schedule security review meeting next week.
[12:24] Dr. Lina Gomez: Sounds good. Thanks, folks.
[12:27] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet and proposed times for a security deep dive.
[12:33] [00:12:33] End meeting.

Notes on transcript quirks: occasional mishearing of KV cache as "K-V cash" and VPC as "V-P-C", small stutters, some speaker attribution shows generic "Speaker 1" for a question at 04:12. Links shared: Security whitepaper: https://redwood.ai/security (shared post-call); Pricing workbook: link to sheet (sent via email).
